title: Rick & Linda in Hakone
og_desc: Typhoon Dujuan passes offshore today. Indoors at Kinnotake Tonosawa, then the full Hakone loop tomorrow.

pre_sections.lead: Japan Meteorological Agency, 6:00 AM Monday. Typhoon No. 25 is 210 km southwest of Hachijojima, moving north-northeast at 20 km/h. Central pressure 965 hPa, sustained winds 35 m/s. It does not make landfall. It passes east of Tokyo, over the sea.
pts: Hakone is on the far side
The strong winds are over Chiba and the Izu Islands. Hakone sits west of the track, about as far from the eye as Kanto gets.
What Hakone actually gets is rain
Heavy, with thunder, from late morning until early evening. The risk here is rain on mountain roads and rail, not wind.
Trains on your route were running normally at 7:12 AM
Tokaido Line, Odakyu Romancecar and the Hakone-Tozan line all on schedule. Every suspension is east of you: Chiba, and a few mountain lines west of Tokyo from the afternoon.
One Hakone bus is out all day
The Odawara sightseeing loop bus "Umemaru-go" is suspended for the whole of Monday. Nothing you need.

pre_sections.lead: Tokyo to Tonosawa is about two hours. Do it before the rain peaks and the rest of the day takes care of itself.
pts: Tokyo or Shinagawa → Odawara
Tokaido Line, roughly 1 hour 20 minutes. The Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku is the other way in.
Odawara → Hakone-Yumoto → Tonosawa
Hakone-Tozan Line. Tonosawa is one stop past Yumoto, and the ryokan is a 3 minute walk from the station.
If the Tozan line stops for rain
Take a taxi from Odawara Station straight to the hotel, about 10 to 15 minutes. Do not wait at the station for a train that may not come.
Check-in and then stop moving
Everything below happens under one roof.

sections.lead: Kinnotake Tonosawa is built into the forest above the Hayakawa river. Every room has its own open-air hot spring bath, so the weather outside is somebody else's problem. Times below are from the ryokan's own site.
pts: Your own open-air bath
Every room at Kinnotake Tonosawa has one. Rain on a private rotenburo is the good version of this day, not the consolation prize.
Private pool and sauna — book it
15:00–22:00, last start 21:00. One party at a time, 60 minutes, ¥3,000 per person. Reserve at the 3rd floor front desk after check-in. Sauna kit free, swimsuit rental ¥3,000.
Gym, open around the clock
Nine machines, free, open 24 hours except 9:30–10:30 for cleaning. Wear ¥1,500 and shoes ¥1,000 to rent if you did not pack any.
The lounge
Drinks and books, looking into the forest. Candles at night.

sections.lead: A converted old house in the grounds, all done by hand. They start by asking how you are and build the treatment from that. Ask the front desk to book as soon as you check in — there are only so many slots and everyone in the building has the same idea today.
pts: Body treatment
60 min ¥22,000 / 90 min ¥28,000 / 120 min ¥35,000. You pick the oil by smell at the start.
Onsen facial
60 min, ¥23,000 basic or ¥26,000 for the aging-care versions. Uses Hakone hot spring water.
Reflexology, fully clothed
60 min ¥20,000. Feet and head. This is the one that puts you to sleep — a good choice after a hard travel day.
ZEN TOJI, the couples course
120 min, ¥84,000 for the two of you. You choose the herbs, soak in a private herbal bath in the detached building, then body and mini-facial. This only exists here.
Add-ons
Private herbal bath 30 min ¥12,000, mini facial 30 min ¥12,000, extra 30 min ¥8,000.

sections.lead: Three ways to eat without going outside, and a bar that opens when the rain has stopped mattering.
pts: Dining room
Seatings at 17:30 or 19:30, closes 21:30. Breakfast at 7:30, 8:00, 8:30 or 9:00, closes 10:00.
Teppanyaki Zen, on the grounds
Seatings 17:00 / 18:00 / 19:00 / 20:00, two and a half hours at the table, closes 22:00. Ishigaki Island premium beef cooked in front of you. Worth booking today rather than tomorrow.
Bar Bamboo
21:00 to midnight, last order 23:30. Whisky, wine, sake, cocktails. ¥1,100 per person cover. One travel listing says the bar is paused, so confirm at the front desk when you check in.

rows: Before the rain peaks. This is the only time-critical thing today.
3 minute walk from the station to the ryokan.
3rd floor front desk. Slots go fast on a rained-in day.
60 minutes, one party at a time.

sections.lead: Tuesday's forecast is cloudy with some sun. The Hakone loop runs anticlockwise on four different kinds of transport and ends back at your door — train, cable car, ropeway, boat, bus. Note that Tuesday Sep 22 is a national holiday in Japan, so holiday timetables apply and it will be busy.
pts: Buy the Hakone Free Pass first

¥6,000 per adult for two days, from Odawara or from Hakone-Yumoto — same price either way. It covers the Tozan train, the Tozan buses on the designated routes, the cable car, the ropeway and the pirate ship. Romancecar limited-express fees are not included.
Tonosawa → Chokoku-no-Mori
Hakone-Tozan Line, 31 to 39 minutes, about four trains an hour in the morning. The switchbacks up the mountain are part of the ride.
Hakone Open-Air Museum
9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30, open every day. ¥2,000 at the gate, ¥1,800 if you buy online first. Sculpture across an open hillside, plus a Picasso building. Give it two hours.

sections.lead: From Gora you change to a funicular, then to a gondola that crosses directly over a live volcanic vent. This is the part people remember.
pts: Gora → Sounzan cable car
11 minutes straight up the hillside.
Sounzan → Owakudani ropeway
About 10 minutes, cars roughly every minute, running 9:00–17:00 in September. On a clear stretch Mt Fuji appears behind you.
Get off at Owakudani

Steam vents, sulphur, and the black eggs — boiled in the hot spring until the shells turn black. ¥500 for four at the Kuro-tamago-kan, sold 9:00–16:40. Local lore says each one adds seven years to your life.
Owakudani → Ubako → Togendai
About 10 minutes each, changing cars at Owakudani. Lake Ashi opens up in front of you on the way down.
The one thing that can close
The ropeway stops at wind speeds of 30 m/s or more, and in bad weather generally. Check the status page over breakfast before you commit to the route.

sections.lead: It is exactly as silly as it sounds, and the view is genuinely the best on the lake. Covered by the Free Pass.
pts: Togendai → Motohakone-ko
The operator puts the Togendai to Hakone-machi / Motohakone crossing at about 25 to 40 minutes. ¥1,200 one way if you were paying, which you are not.
Sit outside if it is dry
Fuji is behind you on the way across, the torii is ahead of you as you come in.
Hakone Shrine, 10 minutes' walk from the pier

Cedar avenue up to the shrine. The amulet office is open 8:15–17:00 and the treasure hall takes visitors 9:00–16:00. Opening hours for the grounds themselves are not published — in practice you walk in.
The torii in the water
The Peace Torii stands in the lake below the shrine. There is usually a queue to stand in front of it. Worth it.

sections.lead: One bus closes the loop. No backtracking, no repeated legs.
pts: Motohakone-ko → Hakone-Yumoto
Hakone-Tozan bus, H route, from stop 1 at the pier. ¥1,210 if you were paying — the Free Pass covers it. Via Ashinoyu and Miyanoshita, down the old mountain road.
Hakone-Yumoto → Tonosawa
One stop on the Tozan line, or a short taxi. Then the bath in your room.
If the ropeway is shut
Skip the mountain and go indoors instead: Pola Museum of Art 9:00–17:00, ¥2,200. Hakone Glass Forest 10:00–17:30, ¥1,800. Okada Museum 9:00–17:00, ¥2,800. All reachable on the Free Pass buses.

rows: Ropeway over the vents. Black eggs, ¥500 for 4.
Stop 1. Then one stop to Tonosawa.

end.lead: Today the weather makes the decision for you and the ryokan is a good place to lose an afternoon. Tomorrow the storm is out at sea and Hakone does what it is famous for. Check the transport status page over breakfast before you set out — that is the only thing that can change the plan.
